title: BUGEM: Fast and Robust Algorithm for Extracting EndMembers in STEM Spectrum-Images
content: Non-negative matrix factorization [1] is a widely used method for simplifying and interpreting complex spectrum-imaging datasets, like STEM Electron Energy-Loss Spectra (EELS) or Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectra (EDS) sets. The method decomposes data onto a small amount of endmember spectra while ensuring that none of the observed data points contain negative contributions from any endmembers. While effective in many cases, the strict non-negativity constraint can cause serious issues when applied to typical STEM EELS and EDS spectrum-images, which are often very noisy. Allowing small negative abundances - provided that they are within the expected noise variance – seems to be more effective practical solution. Several Bayesian models for extracting endmembers have been proposed to address this issue [2,3]. The explicit Bayesian inference is however computationally expensive and prone to convergence problems.
